# Location Optimization

## {.slide data-menu-title="Remember this question?"}

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width='55%'}

Remember this one?

::: {.value-box icon="bi bi-hospital" align="center" icon-size="1.5em"}
What if we opened a new site here?
:::

::: {.fragment}
**Location optimization** is how we answer it properly.

It's the first power tool we hand HSMAs once they've got the mapping fundamentals.
:::

## Flavours of Location Problem

Many geographic problems come down to one of these three things:

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width='33%'}

::: {.value-box value="Expansion"  icon-position="top" align="center" icon="fa-solid fa-circle-plus"}
"I need to **add** a site"

*Where should our new community diagnostic centre go?*

:::

:::

::: {.column width='33%'}

::: {.value-box value="Consolidation" icon-position="top" align="center" icon="fa-solid fa-circle-minus"}

I need to **remove** a site

*Which of our sites do we close when the estate has to shrink?*

:::

:::

::: {.column width='33%' icon-position="top" align="center" icon="fa-brands fa-connectdevelop"}

::: {.value-box value="Network Design"}

I need to work out where to put a *load* of sites where none currently 'exist'

*Where do all the vaccination centres go?*
:::

:::

::::


## Why can't we just eyeball it?

Fourteen candidate sites, and funding for one. That's fourteen options — small enough to list on a whiteboard.

::: {.fragment}
Until the question changes.
:::

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width='33%'}
::: {.value-box value="14" fragment="fade-in"}
Options to weigh up when opening 1 site.
:::
:::

::: {.column width='33%'}
::: {.value-box value="91" fragment="fade-in"}
Options to weigh up when opening 2 sites.
:::
:::

::: {.column width='33%'}
::: {.value-box value="364" fragment="fade-in"}
Options to weigh up when opening 3 sites.
:::
:::

::::

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width='33%'}
::: {.value-box value="1001" fragment="fade-in"}
Options to weigh up when opening 4 sites.
:::
:::

::: {.column width='33%'}
::: {.value-box value="2002" fragment="fade-in"}
Options to weigh up when opening 5 sites.
:::
:::

::: {.column width='33%'}
::: {.value-box value="3003" fragment="fade-in"}
Options to weigh up when opening 6 sites.
:::
:::

::::

::: {.fragment}
Every site you add to the question multiplies the answers.
:::


## And that's the easy part

Each of those options has to be judged against [**several different measures at once**]{style="color:yellow"} — and those measures disagree with each other.

::: {.fragment}

At fourteen options, a patient analyst can at least *build* the table.

:::

::: {.fragment}

Reading it is another matter — fourteen rows, a column for every measure, and no single row that wins on all of them.

:::

::: {.fragment}

And nobody stops at fourteen. The neonatal project we'll look at later chose from **22 candidate sites** — run the same escalation out that far and you're not weighing up hundreds of combinations. You're into the thousands.

:::

::: {.fragment}

::: {.value-box}
**Location Optimization** is the branch of operational research that scores every combination against every measure — and tells you which handful are actually worth arguing about.
:::

:::


## Best at what?

Before it can rank anything, the model has to be told what "best" means.

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width='50%'}
::: {.value-box icon="bi bi-clock-fill" fragment="fade-in" icon-position="left"}
The shortest **average journey**?
:::
:::

::: {.column width='50%'}
::: {.value-box icon="bi bi-people-fill" fragment="fade-in" icon-position="left"}
The most people **within 30 minutes**?
:::
:::

::::

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width='50%'}
::: {.value-box icon="bi bi-exclamation-triangle-fill" fragment="fade-in" icon-position="left"}
The shortest **worst-case journey**?
:::
:::

::: {.column width='50%'}
::: {.value-box icon="bi bi-bar-chart-fill" fragment="fade-in" icon-position="left"}
The shortest journeys for the **most deprived third**?
:::
:::

::::

::: {.value-box icon="bi bi-arrows-collapse" fragment="fade-in" icon-position="left" width="100%"}
The **narrowest gap** between the most and least deprived?
:::

::: {.fragment}

The model doesn't decide which of these matters. [**You**]{style="color:yellow"} do.

:::


## When Objectives Disagree

Say you're choosing a car. You care about two things: **price**, and **boot space**.

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width='33%'}
::: {.value-box fragment="fade-in"}
**Car A**

Cheap. Tiny boot.
:::
:::

::: {.column width='33%'}
::: {.value-box fragment="fade-in"}
**Car B**

Expensive. Huge boot.
:::
:::

::: {.column width='33%'}
::: {.value-box style="opacity: 0.6;" fragment="fade-in"}
**Car C**

Expensive. Tiny boot.
:::
:::

::::

::: {.fragment}
Car A and Car B are both [**defensible**]{style="color:yellow"} — neither beats the other. Each wins on something you might care about.
:::

::: {.fragment}
Car C isn't. Something else beats it on price *and* boot space at once. Nobody would choose it — rule it out.
:::

::: {.fragment}

::: {.value-box}
Today's optimiser does exactly this, across more objectives and many more options. What it hands back isn't one right answer — it's a shortlist of **defensible** ones, like Car A and Car B.
:::

:::


## Decision *Support*, not Decisions

Like most good operational research, this should be treated as *decision support*

It's not telling you the one 'right' answer

It's just more robust evidence to add to

- system knowledge
- patient feedback
- what's actually deliverable

::: {.value-box fragment="fade-in"}

The best site on paper might be the one you can't build on.

And once a service opens, demand you never knew about can appear.

:::


## Questions to Ask Your Analyst

Before you trust a map — or a ranking — some questions are always worth asking.

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width='50%'}
::: {.value-box icon="bi bi-sliders" fragment="fade-in" icon-position="left"}
What was this optimised for — and who chose that?
:::
:::

::: {.column width='50%'}
::: {.value-box icon="bi bi-signpost-fill" fragment="fade-in" icon-position="left"}
Who did the model assume simply can't be reached?
:::
:::

::::

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width='50%'}
::: {.value-box icon="bi bi-car-front-fill" fragment="fade-in" icon-position="left"}
What travel mode, and what time of day, is this based on?
:::
:::

::: {.column width='50%'}
::: {.value-box icon="bi bi-palette-fill" fragment="fade-in" icon-position="left"}
This colour is an average for the whole area. Who does it hide?
:::
:::

::::

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width='50%'}
::: {.value-box icon="bi bi-bounding-box" fragment="fade-in" icon-position="left"}
Would the answer change if the boundaries had been drawn differently?
:::
:::

::: {.column width='50%'}
::: {.value-box icon="bi bi-list-ol" fragment="fade-in" icon-position="left"}
What's the second-best option — and how much worse is it, really?
:::
:::

::::

::: {.fragment}

::: {.value-box}
You won't remember all six. Remember the first: **what was this optimised for, and who chose that?**
:::

:::
